title: A Method to Enrich Functional Human Paneth Cells in Intestinal Organoids
author: Patel, Shachi

steps.title: Generate epithelial‑only organoids
steps.instruction: Purify the epithelial cell fraction from 30‑day iPSC‑derived intestinal organoids (HIOs) and culture them as epithelial‑only HIOs (eHIOs), maintaining the cultures with serial passaging every 7 days.

steps.title: Prepare modified maintenance media
steps.instruction: Make basal medium containing EGF 100 ng/mL, Noggin 100 ng/mL, and CHIR99021 3 µM (increase from 2 µM). Omit the small‑molecule inhibitors SB202190 (10 µM) and A83‑01 (500 nM). Add DAPT to a final concentration of 10 µM. For comparison, a parallel formulation may include IL‑22 at 2 ng/mL.

steps.title: Culture eHIOs in modified media
steps.instruction: Place eHIOs in the modified ENC(3)+DAPT medium, incubate under standard organoid conditions, and passage the cultures weekly (every 7 days).

steps.title: Cytokine stimulation (optional)
steps.instruction: Treat eHIOs with recombinant IL‑22 at 10 ng/mL for 5 days to assess functional responsiveness.

steps.title: Seed eHIOs onto Transwell inserts
steps.instruction: Dissociate eHIOs into single cells or small clusters, plate them onto collagen‑coated Transwell inserts, and culture until a confluent monolayer forms, preserving Paneth cell enrichment.

steps.title: Stimulate monolayers with microbial ligands
steps.instruction: Apply the following ligands to the apical compartment: NOD2 ligand MDP (concentration as used in the study), Pam3CSK4, Flagellin, and LPS (concentrations as used in the study). Incubate for the appropriate time and measure lysozyme secretion (e.g., by ELISA).

steps.title: Co‑culture live patient bacteria
steps.instruction: Add live bacterial suspensions obtained from resected ileocolonic tissue to the apical side of the Transwell monolayers, incubate for 30 minutes, then collect apical and basolateral media for secreted protein analysis by mass spectrometry or ELISA.
